detailed_description: The JSONPath Tester evaluates a simple path expression against pasted JSON in the browser. Paste JSON, enter a basic path such as `$.name`, `$.users[0]`, or `$.users[0].name`, click Evaluate, and review the formatted result or error message. The current parser removes a leading `$` or `$.`, then walks dot-separated object properties and bracket array indexes. Example buttons fill common paths, and successful results can be copied. The tool does not implement full JSONPath syntax such as wildcards, filters, array slicing, recursive descent, raw-output modes, match highlighting, collapsible trees, URI import, query validation panels, or JSON/CSV downloads.
usage_steps: Paste valid JSON into the JSON data textarea.
Enter a simple path using object properties and array indexes.
Use an example button if you want to start from a common path format.
Click Evaluate and review the formatted result or error message.
Copy the result when the selected value is useful.
usage_examples: Read a top-level value with a path like `$.name`.
Inspect the first item in an array with a path like `$.users[0]`.
Extract a nested value such as `$.users[0].name` from a small sample object.
Copy the formatted selected value for manual debugging notes.
